texts.li: [lowtech] A traveler brought {A_nameDef} word from the people {A_pronoun} left behind: a baby was born there this spring, and they named the child after {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} made the traveler say it twice.
[!lowtech] A short letter has caught up with {A_nameDef} after months on the road. Someone from {A_possessive} old life has had a child and named it after {A_nameDef}, "for luck," the letter says.
[soldier] Word has come from one of {A_nameDef}'s old comrades: the first child of the family has {A_nameDef}'s name, after the night {A_nameDef} carried {A_possessive} comrade back to the lines.
[healer] A family {A_nameDef} once nursed through a fever has sent word: their new baby is named after {A_objective}. The letter came with a lock of very fine hair.
[farmer] The neighbors from the old farm have had a child, and named it after {A_nameDef}. The news came with a sack of seed from the old fields, as a gift.
[outlaw] Of all the people {A_nameDef} knew in the bad old days, one went straight, married, and has named a child after {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} isn't sure whether to be proud or worried.

[lowtech] A peddler brought {A_nameDef} a wedding invitation, folded small and much traveled. The wedding was two seasons ago. Someone {A_nameDef} grew up with married, and wanted {A_objective} there.

[!lowtech] An invitation to a wedding has reached {A_nameDef}, five months late and stamped by every relay between here and home. A friend from {A_possessive} old life got married, and kept a seat for {A_objective}.
[noble] A sealed letter has reached {A_nameDef}: a cousin has married into one of the great houses, and the family thought {A_nameDef} should know. There's a pressed flower from the wedding inside.

[trader] Word came with a caravan that {A_nameDef}'s old trading partner finally married the innkeeper's daughter, after nine years of saying {A_pronoun} never would. {A_nameDef} laughed until {A_pronoun} had to sit down.
{A_nameDef} has heard, late and secondhand, that an old friend from before the colony got married this year. The friend sent a message, and the message found its way here.

[Crafting] A trader passing through had a knife {A_nameDef} made years ago, before the colony, and recognized the maker's mark. The trader says people on the road still ask where to get another one like it.
[Construction] A traveler told {A_nameDef} that a bridge {A_pronoun} helped build, a long way from here, is still standing after a flood that took every other bridge on the river.

[Artistic] A visitor described a carving in a town square far from here, and {A_nameDef} realized halfway through that it was {A_possessive} own, made years ago. People still leave flowers at its foot.

[Cooking] A traveler asked {A_nameDef} if {A_pronoun} was the cook from a certain inn on the coast road. They still serve {A_possessive} stew there, under {A_possessive} name, and the traveler had eaten it.
[Medicine] A trader stopped to tell {A_nameDef} that a patient {A_pronoun} once stitched up on the road is alive and well, and tells everyone about the healer who saved the leg.
[Plants] A traveler mentioned that the orchard {A_nameDef} planted long ago, far from here, has finally come into fruit. The village sends its thanks, a little late.

[Shooting|Melee] A traveler recognized {A_nameDef} from an old tournament and said people still argue about that final round. {A_nameDef} said it was a long time ago, and then told the whole story anyway.
[Intellectual] A trader brought news that a paper {A_nameDef} wrote years ago, on {SKILL}, is still copied and passed around. Someone has added notes in the margins, mostly arguing with it.
[Social] A traveler told {A_nameDef} that a quarrel {A_pronoun} once settled between two villages is still settled, and both of them still tell the story of how.
[Animals] A herder passing through said a breed of dog {A_nameDef} raised years ago has spread up and down the valley, and they still call them by {A_nameDef}'s name.
A traveler recognized {A_nameDef}'s name from the old days. Something {A_nameDef} did with {SKILL}, years ago and far from here, is still talked about on the road.

[lowtech,notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} travels alone with a handcart of masks and a drum, and plays every part in the show {X_pronoun} carries from town to town. {X_nameDef} would like supper and a dry place to sleep, and will perform after dark.

[lowtech,tale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a mummer who plays every part {X_pronoun} so much as hears about, has made a play out of what people say about this colony on the road: "{TALE}" {X_nameDef} would like to perform it tonight, for supper and a bed.

[!lowtech,notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is a traveling player with a painted backdrop rolled up on {X_possessive} back and a play with eleven parts, all of them {X_possessive}. {X_nameDef} will perform it tonight in exchange for supper and somewhere to sleep.

[!lowtech,tale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} performs short plays in every settlement on the road, and has written one about the colony from a story going around: "{TALE}" {X_nameDef} would like to try it out tonight, on an audience who know how it really went.

[winter,notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a traveling player, came in out of the snow with {X_possessive} costumes in a sack. {X_nameDef} will perform tonight, if the colony will feed {X_objective} and let {X_objective} sleep somewhere warm.
[summer,notale] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has set up a stage of two planks and a blanket in the yard, in the long light after supper. All {X_nameDef} asks is a meal and a place to sleep.

lines.li: Louder, for the ones at the back!
